content: No man can rob you of your will.
author: Marcus Aurelius
story:
At its core, this reflection cuts through our everyday excuses. From childhood, we are trained to fit in, to smooth over our eccentricities, and to mirror the expectations of those around us. But copying others only buys superficial acceptance at the cost of your own soul.

In Marcus Aurelius's view, genuine strength is not an abstract theory—it is a lived, daily practice. Your unique perspective and lived contradictions are your greatest offering to the world. The moment you stop performing and stand firmly in your own skin, you command an authority that imitation can never manufacture.
reflectionPrompt: When you look back on past hardships, how did navigating them expand your capacity for strength?
